Ethan (Support): :rotating_light: ACME (customer) reporting repeated 502/504s to hosted API gateway starting ~2026-03-15T16:12:04Z. They see spikes on POST /v1/generate and /v1/streams. First noticed after a traffic burst from a background job.
Priya (SRE): Can you paste an example request/trace id? Are these always at the edge or sometimes in the backend?
Ethan (Support): They provided this trace id: trace=tr_0a9f3b7e. Sample logs: 
```
[envoy] 2026-03-15T16:12:05Z outgoing 502 upstream reset stream_id=12345 trace=tr_0a9f3b7e x-forwarded-for=52.12.34.56
[nginx] 2026-03-15T16:12:05Z 502 "upstream prematurely closed connection" client=52.12.34.56 request="POST /v1/streams"
```
ACME-app: throwing stack: "Error: upstream closed before headers" and report of ~350 requests failing in 2m window.
Priya (SRE): Looks like upstream (auth or runtime) connection reset. Can you collect headers they sent, especially `x-client-id`, `authorization`, and `content-length`? Also the backend pod logs around same trace.
Ethan (Support): Sent headers they logged: `x-client-id: acme-job-12`, `authorization: Bearer redacted`, `content-type: application/json`, `te: trailers`. They said traffic is gRPC->HTTP/2 multiplexing from their side.
Marta (Account): ACME is on a high-volume nightly job; we promised <1% errors. They're escalating to CSM. 
ops-bot: Noted. Auto-escalation created: INC-2026-2187.
deploy-bot: Canary 2026-03-15T15:50 rolled to runtime v1.13.2 on hosted cluster region-us-west-2. No failed deploys.
Priya (SRE): Two initial hypotheses: 1) h2 connection pool exhaustion at Envoy due to long-lived streaming requests => early connection resets; 2) an auth-proxy Thundering Herd / backend circuit breaker triggered causing 502s.
Ethan (Support): Customer verified they saw higher tail latencies just before errors. They can reproduce with a small script. Provided curl (simplified):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-x","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/streams
```
Priya (SRE): Repro steps for us: 1) run 200 concurrent short streaming calls from same client id 2) observe envoy/ingress metrics: `envoy_http2_external.active_streams`, `upstream_cx_active`, `upstream_cx_overflow`.
Ethan (Support): I pulled metrics around the incident window:
```
metric: envoy_http2_external.active_streams = 420 (95th),
metric: upstream_cx_active = 280,
metric: upstream_cx_overflow = spikes to 40 in bursts
```
Priya (SRE): That overflow spike is consistent with pool exhaustion. Also check `envoy_http_downstream_rq_5xx` and `envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_completed`.
Priya (SRE): Quick mitigations: 1) Temporarily increase Envoy `max_concurrent_streams` / connection pool size for affected cluster; 2) enable short-term connection draining on long-polling customers (ACME agreed to reduce concurrency); 3) add an edge-level rate limiter for same `x-client-id` to protect backend.
Marta (Account): ACME willing to stagger their job over 30m window. They need instructions to change concurrency.
Ethan (Support): Implemented temporary rate-limit rule for `acme-job-12` at 200 RPS via edge policies (applied at 16:30 UTC).
ops-bot: Policy applied: edge-rate-limit acme-job-12 = 200rps (scope: region-us-west-2).
ACME-app: After the throttle they report errors dropped by 95%, but still occasional 502s at tail.
Priya (SRE): For root cause we need: a) backend auth-proxy trace for the trace id, b) Envoy logs with `upstream reset` reason (connection termination vs timeout), c) whether runtime worker OOM / slow KV cache.
Ethan (Support): Grabbed more runtime logs near trace=tr_0a9f3b7e: 
```
[runtime] 2026-03-15T16:12:04Z worker-13 worker stalled handling request id=req_7f8a authcache_miss=true kv_fetch_ms=1200
[runtime] 2026-03-15T16:12:05Z worker-13 closed connection upstream reset ECONNABORTED
```
Priya (SRE): That kv_fetch_ms=1200 looks suspicious for auth cache. Could be a downstream LDAP/KMS or auth service latency causing long head-of-line blocking on streaming workers. Follow-up: check auth-proxy latency and circuit breaker logs.
Ethan (Support): Auth team confirms a transient spike to their DB at 16:11 causing auth latencies ~1.2s for some keys; they retried behind a bulkhead.
Priya (SRE): So combined picture: customer sent many long-lived h2 streams; envoys exhausted h2 stream slots while auth cache misses increased backend latency, causing upstream connections to be closed -> 502s. Multi-factor.
Marta (Account): Communicated root-cause to ACME. They've asked for a post-mortem and SLO credit.
Priya (SRE): Action items:
- [P1] Increase edge h2 pool limits + monitor (Priya)
- [P2] Add per-client concurrent stream rate limiting in edge (Ethan + Priya)
- [P3] Auth team to add local LRU cache and backoff to reduce kv_fetch tail (Auth team)
- [P4] Run chaos test for h2 long-lived stream scenarios (SRE + Eng-runtime)
- [P5] Postmortem write-up and customer SLO compensation proposal (Marta)

Ethan (Support): Assigning P1->Priya, P2->Ethan, P5->Marta. ETA P1 24h, P2 48h, P5 72h.
Priya (SRE): I'll create a follow-up runbook entry for `edge/h2-pool-exhaustion` with reproduction steps and mitigations.
Marta (Account): ACME acknowledges and appreciates the quick mitigation. :pray:
Ethan (Support): Closing thread for real-time triage. Will re-open if errors re-appear.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-2187 moved to status: monitoring."
